notice_text: The Government of Botswana is undertaking the Promoting Participation and Enhancing Learning (PROPEL) (P513800) project supported by the World Bank.   The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase participation in preprimary and senior secondary education and improve learning conditions in supported schools, particularly at the junior secondary level. The Project consists of the following four components: Component 1: Increasing participation in education Component 2: Enhancing the learning environment Component 3: Strengthening system capacity for quality education service delivery  Component 4: Project management and implementation support   The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education (MCWBE) is the implementing entity for the Project. A Project Delivery Unit (PDU) (or Program Coordinating Unit) is being established within MCWBE to support the effective implementation of project activities, including procurement and contract administration; monitoring, evaluation and reporting of progress under the project; fiduciary management; and environmental and social safeguards management. Specifically, the PDU will be responsible for ensuring that implementation of social risk management activities is conducted in an efficient, transparent, and compliant manner. To strengthen implementation capacity and support timely delivery, the MCWBE seeks to engage an Individual Social Development Consultant as a core member of the PDU.   The objective of this assignment is to ensure that project activities comply with relevant national regulatory requirements as well as the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and applicable Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs). This includes identifying and mitigating potential social risks, instrument preparation, monitoring, and reporting, overseeing stakeholder engagement and grievance redress processes, and building the capacity of MCWBE to manage social issues effectively throughout project implementation.   The Social Development Consultant will perform duties that include, but are not limited to, the following: Social Risk Management: (i) Support PDU in establishing social risk management systems, screening tools, and procedures in line with Project Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) requirements, including contributions to the Project Operations Manual (POM); (ii) lead or support the preparation of E&S instruments required under the ESCP and oversee fulfillment of ESF commitments, review site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), conduct field visits, and maintain supervision records; and (iii) ensure E&S requirements (ESMP, LMP, Code of Conduct) are reflected in bidding documents and contracts prior to issuance; review contractor-submitted E&S plans and verify implementation on site.  Gender Based Violence (GBV) and SEA/SH (Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment): Work closely with the GBV Specialist on the development and implementation of the SEA/SH Action Plan, and its integration into project activities. Stakeholder Engagement: Implement the Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), lead consultations with stakeholders including communities, schools, and government partners, and ensure inclusion of vulnerable groups. Grievance Redress Mechanism: Facilitate establishment and operation of an accessible GRM, with appropriate channels to receive SEA/SH complaints, monitor resolution of complaints, and ensure confidential handling of SEA/SH cases, including adequate dissemination of information regarding GRM reporting channels to stakeholders and affected communities. Labor and Working Conditions: Monitor contractor compliance with Labor Management Procedures (LMP) under ESS2. Monitoring, Reporting, and Capacity Building: Prepare quarterly monitoring reports, contribute to mid-term and final evaluations, and strengthen capacity for MCWBE staff, school administrators, and project partners on E&S requirements. Develop guidance notes, checklists, and practical tools to support social risk management of the project. Perform any other related tasks assigned by the supervisor within the scope of the assignment.   The Social Development Consultant will work as an integral member of the PDU and report to the Project Coordinator. The Social Development Consultant will work in close day-to-day coordination with the Environmental Consultant, GBV Consultant and other PDU staff and will maintain regular communication with the MCWBE and the World Bank Social Specialist assigned to the project.   The duration of the assignment is an initial period of 2 years from contract signature with a probationary period of three (3) months. A formal performance evaluation shall be conducted at the end of the first twelve (12) months by the MCWBE evaluation committee. Continuation of the contract for the second year shall be subject to a satisfactory performance assessment and availability of project funding. The performance assessment will consider, among other factors, the quality and timeliness of deliverables, compliance with the Terms of Reference, and overall effectiveness in supporting project implementation. After the initial period of 2 years, the contract will be renewable for the duration of the project based on satisfactory performance and project needs. The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.   The Social Development Consultant shall have the following minimum qualifications: Master's degree in social sciences, sociology, anthropology, social work, gender studies, development studies, human geography or another relevant discipline. Advanced training or specialization in areas such as social risk management, stakeholder engagement; training in gender and social inclusion will be an added advantage. At least 5 years of relevant professional experience in social development, social safeguards, or related fields in the context of development projects. Proven experience with infrastructure projects, with education sector experience being highly desirable. Demonstrated experience with social sustainability issues in education sector or infrastructure projects, including gender mainstreaming, GBV prevention and response, inclusion of vulnerable groups, stakeholder engagement, and community grievance redress mechanisms. Experience implementing and monitoring social risk management instruments (Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), Resettlement Action Plan (RAP), Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM)) in projects financed by the World Bank or other international financial institutions. Solid understanding of the Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs). Experience working in Botswana or the Southern Africa sub-region is strongly desirable. Familiarity with Botswana's national legislation on social protection, gender, labor, and child welfare is an advantage. Ability and willingness to undertake regular field travel. Strong analytical, communication, and report-writing skills in English and Setswana. Excellent interpersonal and facilitation skills, with demonstrated ability to engage diverse stakeholders including government officials, school communities, civil society, and vulnerable groups. Computer literacy, including proficiency in standard office software and data management tools.   The position offers competitive remuneration for the selected individual. The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section 111, paragraphs 3.14,3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IFP Borrowers (February 2025 version), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. The selection will be made in accordance with the “World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (July 2016) revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 & September 2025. Candidates who meet the required qualifications will be assessed based on the following evaluation criteria. The first ranked candidate will be invited for contract negotiations.   Criterion Points General Qualifications 30 Adequacy for the Assignment 60 English Language Proficiency 10 Total 100   Further information, including the full Terms of Reference, can be obtained at the address below during office hours from Monday to Friday, 0800 hours to 1630 hours (local time). Expressions of interest must be delivered in written form to the address below, whether in person, by mail, or by email, no later than 30th October 2026 at 1600 hours (local time). The Government of Botswana is undertaking the Promoting Participation and Enhancing Learning (PROPEL) (P513800) project supported by the World Bank.

 

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase participation in preprimary and senior secondary education and improve learning conditions in supported schools, particularly at the junior secondary level. The Project consists of the following four components:

  • Component 1: Increasing participation in education
  • Component 2: Enhancing the learning environment
  • Component 3: Strengthening system capacity for quality education service delivery 
  • Component 4: Project management and implementation support

 

The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education (MCWBE) is the implementing entity for the Project. A Project Delivery Unit (PDU) (or Program Coordinating Unit) is being established within MCWBE to support the effective implementation of project activities, including procurement and contract administration; monitoring, evaluation and reporting of progress under the project; fiduciary management; and environmental and social safeguards management. Specifically, the PDU will be responsible for ensuring that implementation of social risk management activities is conducted in an efficient, transparent, and compliant manner. To strengthen implementation capacity and support timely delivery, the MCWBE seeks to engage an Individual Social Development Consultant as a core member of the PDU.

 

The objective of this assignment is to ensure that project activities comply with relevant national regulatory requirements as well as the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and applicable Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs). This includes identifying and mitigating potential social risks, instrument preparation, monitoring, and reporting, overseeing stakeholder engagement and grievance redress processes, and building the capacity of MCWBE to manage social issues effectively throughout project implementation.

 

The Social Development Consultant will perform duties that include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Social Risk Management: (i) Support PDU in establishing social risk management systems, screening tools, and procedures in line with Project Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) requirements, including contributions to the Project Operations Manual (POM); (ii) lead or support the preparation of E&S instruments required under the ESCP and oversee fulfillment of ESF commitments, review site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), conduct field visits, and maintain supervision records; and (iii) ensure E&S requirements (ESMP, LMP, Code of Conduct) are reflected in bidding documents and contracts prior to issuance; review contractor-submitted E&S plans and verify implementation on site. 
  • Gender Based Violence (GBV) and SEA/SH (Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment): Work closely with the GBV Specialist on the development and implementation of the SEA/SH Action Plan, and its integration into project activities.
  • Stakeholder Engagement: Implement the Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), lead consultations with stakeholders including communities, schools, and government partners, and ensure inclusion of vulnerable groups.
  • Grievance Redress Mechanism: Facilitate establishment and operation of an accessible GRM, with appropriate channels to receive SEA/SH complaints, monitor resolution of complaints, and ensure confidential handling of SEA/SH cases, including adequate dissemination of information regarding GRM reporting channels to stakeholders and affected communities.
  • Labor and Working Conditions: Monitor contractor compliance with Labor Management Procedures (LMP) under ESS2.
  • Monitoring, Reporting, and Capacity Building: Prepare quarterly monitoring reports, contribute to mid-term and final evaluations, and strengthen capacity for MCWBE staff, school administrators, and project partners on E&S requirements. Develop guidance notes, checklists, and practical tools to support social risk management of the project.
  • Perform any other related tasks assigned by the supervisor within the scope of the assignment.

 

The Social Development Consultant will work as an integral member of the PDU and report to the Project Coordinator. The Social Development Consultant will work in close day-to-day coordination with the Environmental Consultant, GBV Consultant and other PDU staff and will maintain regular communication with the MCWBE and the World Bank Social Specialist assigned to the project.

 

The duration of the assignment is an initial period of 2 years from contract signature with a probationary period of three (3) months. A formal performance evaluation shall be conducted at the end of the first twelve (12) months by the MCWBE evaluation committee. Continuation of the contract for the second year shall be subject to a satisfactory performance assessment and availability of project funding. The performance assessment will consider, among other factors, the quality and timeliness of deliverables, compliance with the Terms of Reference, and overall effectiveness in supporting project implementation. After the initial period of 2 years, the contract will be renewable for the duration of the project based on satisfactory performance and project needs. The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.

 

The Social Development Consultant shall have the following minimum qualifications:

  • Master's degree in social sciences, sociology, anthropology, social work, gender studies, development studies, human geography or another relevant discipline.
  • Advanced training or specialization in areas such as social risk management, stakeholder engagement; training in gender and social inclusion will be an added advantage.
  • At least 5 years of relevant professional experience in social development, social safeguards, or related fields in the context of development projects.
  • Proven experience with infrastructure projects, with education sector experience being highly desirable.
  • Demonstrated experience with social sustainability issues in education sector or infrastructure projects, including gender mainstreaming, GBV prevention and response, inclusion of vulnerable groups, stakeholder engagement, and community grievance redress mechanisms.
  • Experience implementing and monitoring social risk management instruments (Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), Resettlement Action Plan (RAP), Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM)) in projects financed by the World Bank or other international financial institutions.
  • Solid understanding of the Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs).
  • Experience working in Botswana or the Southern Africa sub-region is strongly desirable.
  • Familiarity with Botswana's national legislation on social protection, gender, labor, and child welfare is an advantage.
  • Ability and willingness to undertake regular field travel.
  • Strong analytical, communication, and report-writing skills in English and Setswana.
  • Excellent interpersonal and facilitation skills, with demonstrated ability to engage diverse stakeholders including government officials, school communities, civil society, and vulnerable groups.
  • Computer literacy, including proficiency in standard office software and data management tools.

 

The position offers competitive remuneration for the selected individual.

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section 111, paragraphs 3.14,3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IFP Borrowers (February 2025 version), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The selection will be made in accordance with the “World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (July 2016) revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 & September 2025.

The Government of Botswana is undertaking the Promoting Participation and Enhancing Learning (PROPEL) (P513800) project supported by the World Bank.

 

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase participation in preprimary and senior secondary education and improve learning conditions in supported schools, particularly at the junior secondary level. The Project consists of the following four components:

  • Component 1: Increasing participation in education
  • Component 2: Enhancing the learning environment
  • Component 3: Strengthening system capacity for quality education service delivery 
  • Component 4: Project management and implementation support

 

The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education (MCWBE) is the implementing entity for the Project. A Project Delivery Unit (PDU) (or Program Coordinating Unit) is being established within MCWBE to support the effective implementation of project activities, including procurement and contract administration; monitoring, evaluation and reporting of progress under the project; fiduciary management; and environmental and social safeguards management. Specifically, the PDU will be responsible for ensuring that implementation of social risk management activities is conducted in an efficient, transparent, and compliant manner. To strengthen implementation capacity and support timely delivery, the MCWBE seeks to engage an Individual Social Development Consultant as a core member of the PDU.

 

The objective of this assignment is to ensure that project activities comply with relevant national regulatory requirements as well as the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and applicable Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs). This includes identifying and mitigating potential social risks, instrument preparation, monitoring, and reporting, overseeing stakeholder engagement and grievance redress processes, and building the capacity of MCWBE to manage social issues effectively throughout project implementation.

  • Gender Based Violence (GBV) and SEA/SH (Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment): Work closely with the GBV Specialist on the development and implementation of the SEA/SH Action Plan, and its integration into project activities.
